task.title: Automatic memory hygiene
task.source: Direct user request to reject low-value memories before collection and automate all tidying.
task.classification: cross-boundary memory capture, persistent storage, background work, remote runtime, and recovery

coreClaim: Automatic capture rejects low-value candidates before persistence, durable background maintenance tidies eligible chat and canonical memories without user action, and each applied batch remains atomically undoable.
rootCause: Capture previously persisted transcript and canonical candidates before value review, while tidying was a manual UI workflow with no durable background job owner.

inScope: Pre-persistence value review for transcript and canonical capture candidates
Bounded startup sweep and automatic background processing
Automatic apply for chat, scene, and character scopes
Exact newest-first undo for consecutive cleanup batches
outOfScope: Automatic cleanup of user, world, or agent canonical scopes
Changing the user's memory-recall enablement preference

claimBoundary.coreClaim: Only active in-scope automatic candidates and stored memories are reviewed; low-value capture candidates never reach storage, and stored cleanup uses recoverable status transitions with exact batch history.
entrypoints: Material chat and canonical memory writes
currentPathsOrFormats: Version 2 memory-capture jobs with two-phase transcript preview and commit
memory-maintenance-jobs coalesced by store and scope
Version 1 and version 2 cleanup apply contracts
Chat memories embedded in chat rows
legacyPathsOrFormats: Valid user, world, and agent canonical memories remain writable but do not enqueue unsupported maintenance
Optional chat cleanup fields restore to their exact prior presence or absence
Manual, imported, corrected, command-created, and pinned status is not low-value evidence by itself
outOfScopeClaims: No provider is claimed to make infallible subjective value judgments.
Deleted cleanup rows are not physically purged.
Unsupported canonical scopes are preserved without automatic maintenance.

contractLaneGate.brokenContract: The old capture path wrote before value review and the old cleanup path required a human to analyze, select, and apply.
contractLaneGate.producer: Engine generation creates capture candidates and cleanup proposals; Rust storage creates durable maintenance jobs at material write boundaries.
contractLaneGate.consumer: Chat and canonical recall, startup background workers, embedded Tauri, and the hostable HTTP runtime.
contractLaneGate.impliedContract: Low-value automatic candidates should never become durable memory, while already stored eligible memories should converge automatically without blocking foreground generation or losing recoverability.
contractLaneGate.actualEnforcement: Two-phase capture previews before model review and commits only accepted transcript candidates; accepted canonical candidates persist after the same gate; storage mutations enqueue coalesced jobs; foreground generation defers workers; bounded workers apply selected proposals and preserve exact undo snapshots.
contractLaneGate.primaryOwnerDetail: src/engine owns value policy and worker orchestration, src-tauri owns durable jobs and atomic persistence, src/shared/api owns typed embedded and remote adapters, and React only mounts startup and optional recovery surfaces.
contractLaneGate.wrongLaneFixToAvoid: Do not hide low-value rows only in React, run durable storage mutation directly from components, or bypass the typed remote dispatch boundary.
regressionProof: Capture tests prove rejected candidates are never committed or created and accepted candidates retain idempotent retry behavior.
Maintenance queue tests prove startup bounds, coalescing, foreground priority, retry, fixed-point convergence, and automatic apply.
Rust tests prove both storage owners, stale atomicity, durable jobs, exact newest-first undo, and lexical-index restoration.
Remote-runtime tests and the isolated ARM64 Pi /api/invoke harness prove hostable command parity.

riskClaimMatrix.coreClaim: Automatic rejection and tidying never require a user click, and recoverable cleanup remains exact.
riskClaimMatrix.riskType: automatic persistent mutation with model-assisted selection
positiveRowsTested: Accepted transcript candidate commits after value review
Accepted canonical consequence persists after value review
Startup and material writes converge through automatic apply
Consecutive chat and canonical batches undo newest first
Remote ARM64 chat and canonical apply and undo succeed
negativeRowsTested: Rejected transcript candidate is never committed
Rejected canonical consequence is never created
Foreground generation prevents background model work
Stale batches cause no partial mutation
User, world, and agent scopes remain valid without unsupported jobs

groundTruthFacts.description: A rejected automatic candidate has no durable memory row.
groundTruthFacts.evidence: Focused capture queue tests assert no transcript commit and no canonical create for rejected candidates.

groundTruthFacts.description: Cleanup undo restores the immediately previous row state, including pre-existing cleanup metadata.
groundTruthFacts.evidence: Chat and canonical consecutive-batch tests undo newest first and compare restored owner records.

positiveRows.claim: The complete frontend behavior remains green.
positiveRows.evidence: pnpm test passed 453 files plus one skipped file, with 2,443 tests passed and one skipped.

positiveRows.claim: The complete Rust storage/runtime behavior remains green.
positiveRows.evidence: cargo test -- --test-threads=1 passed all 1,397 tests; the default parallel run passed 1,396 and exposed one unrelated shared-temp permission race that passed in isolation and serialized.

positiveRows.claim: Architecture, security, storage contracts, docs, discovery, Rust workspace checks, and production compilation remain valid.
positiveRows.evidence: pnpm check and pnpm build passed; changed-file Prettier, cargo fmt, and git diff --check passed.

positiveRows.claim: The hostable ARM64 runtime executes both cleanup owners correctly.
positiveRows.evidence: An isolated exact-source ARM64 Pi server image passed synthetic two-batch apply and undo through /api/invoke for chat and canonical stores without touching production data.

contradictionRows.claim: Low-value candidates must not be briefly stored and removed later.
contradictionRows.evidence: Two-phase capture tests inspect commit/create calls and prove rejection occurs before either storage write.

contradictionRows.claim: Background tidying must not compete with a foreground response.
contradictionRows.evidence: Shared foreground coordinator tests and both automatic queues prove deferral and wake-up behavior.

contradictionRows.claim: Automatic cleanup must not make valid non-maintained canonical scopes unwritable.
contradictionRows.evidence: scoped_query_filters_all_supported_scopes passes for user, character, chat, scene, world, and agent.

legacyDefaultRows.evidence: Legacy/default operation paths and exact prior metadata restoration pass in both storage owners.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Chat expunge clears the new durable job collection.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: Admin expunge scope and complete receipt tests include memory-maintenance-jobs.

untestedRows: Production deployment is intentionally pending until this exact revision merges and its Pi images are published.

ownedFacts.description: The two-phase storage capability, not the retired one-phase refresh method, is the automatic-capture availability boundary.
ownedFacts.evidence: Group-generation tests pass with previewChatMemoryCapture and commitChatMemoryCapture and no refreshChatMemories implementation.

ownedFacts.description: Only chat, scene, and character scopes receive automatic maintenance jobs.
ownedFacts.evidence: Rust job and canonical scope tests preserve all supported canonical scopes while enqueueing only maintained scopes.

userActionCopy.description: Automatic cleanup is recoverable through its retained undo history, so no backup is required for normal operation. For an optional external copy before enabling this version, export a full profile backup.
userActionCopy.destination: A user-selected folder outside De-Koi's application data directory
userActionCopy.action: Save the exported backup before updating De-Koi if an independent copy is desired.

verification.baselineCommand: pnpm test; cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --test-threads=1; pnpm check; pnpm build
verification.baselineEvidence: 2,443 frontend tests, 1,397 Rust tests, deterministic repository checks, Rust workspace check, production build, changed-file formatting, rustfmt, and diff whitespace all passed.

notes: No real user memory content is included in this ledger.
The ARM64 Pi proof used synthetic isolated storage and removed its temporary container, volume, image, and worktree afterward.
Production Pi data was not modified during pre-merge validation.
Repository-wide Prettier reports 305 baseline files; every file changed by this branch passes Prettier.
Bunny reviewed the current diff across capture, storage ownership, startup scheduling, remote dispatch, recovery, and consumer boundaries with no unresolved findings.
The simplification audit found no confirmed behavior-preserving reductions: the new capability, entity adapters, durable job model, and startup worker each have concrete cross-boundary consumers.
